text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.04% today to $389.44, continuing a choppy two-week decline. The stock has faced headwinds from talk of a potential U.S. diesel export ban—a policy that would likely hurt refiners by forcing them to sell more fuel domestically at lower prices while global diesel shortages push international prices higher, squeezing their margins. Additionally, escalating Iran tensions (with reports of Trump rejecting ceasefire proposals and expecting renewed bombing after midterms) add uncertainty to crude supplies and refining economics.

The broader refinery backdrop is mixed: U.S. refineries are running at a solid 94% capacity, but oil inventories remain elevated at 711 million barrels while diesel stocks sit at 107 million barrels—suggesting refiners aren't operating under acute supply pressure that would help them command better prices. The geopolitical risk and policy uncertainty appear to be weighing more heavily on the stock than current operational conditions.
